direction: Candlelit Cellar Editorial — a moody, dark-mode wine journal where deep oxblood meets tallow-cream typography, set on a warm aubergine-black canvas with hand-drawn marginalia energy.
rationale: Vespera is candlelit, earthy, and conversational — the opposite of the cold-white sommelier websites. We lean into a dark, warm, almost zine-like editorial feel: oversized italic serif headlines like a wine label, mono kickers like cellar tags, and a single deep-red glow that mimics candlelight on a bottle. It reads warm and human, not curated-to-death.

palette.note: OKLCH-thought palette: aubergine-black base (oklch ~0.2 0.02 25), tallow cream text (oklch ~0.92 0.03 75), oxblood primary (oklch ~0.38 0.14 20), beeswax accent (oklch ~0.78 0.12 65). Interpolated in oklch so the red-to-amber candle glow stays warm, never muddy.

fonts.pairingNote: Fraunces with opsz pushed to 144 and a soft italic axis for headlines — gives a hand-set wine-label warmth. Inter Tight (NOT default Inter) for body sits quietly underneath. JetBrains Mono for tiny kicker tags and vintage years.

type.displayTreatment: Oversized Fraunces italic at clamp(3rem, 7.5vw, 7rem), line-height 0.94, letter-spacing -0.04em. One word per headline gets a true italic swash accent (e.g., 'natural wine, *honestly*'). Mono UPPERCASE kickers at 0.72rem, tracking 0.24em, preceded by a 32px beeswax hairline.
type.scaleNote: Editorial scale: huge display, generous mid-size pull quotes at ~1.5rem italic, body at 1.0625rem with 1.6 leading. Numerals (vintages, bottle counts) get tabular-nums and oversized serif treatment as section markers — '01 / pour', '02 / shop'.

spacing.rhythmNote: Sections breathe — 8rem vertical rhythm on desktop. Tone bands alternate aubergine-black, slightly warmer plum, and a near-black inverted band for the tasting CTA. Content columns capped at 62ch so paragraphs feel like a letter, not a brochure.

motion.note: Candle-flicker: a single hero glow gently shifts opacity 0.85↔1 over 6s. Section reveals fade + 20px rise, staggered 80ms, cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1). Bottle cards tilt 1.5° on hover with a warm amber glow. Honors prefers-reduced-motion fully.

signatureDevices: OKLCH candle-glow hero: single oxblood-to-beeswax radial wash in the lower-left, one blurred amber orb top-right, hairline rule across the fold — restraint over blob fields
Hairline-bento bottle grid: 1px-gap grid on border color, each cell a bottle with vintage as oversized serif numeral, producer in mono kicker, tasting note in italic body
Oversized section numerals ('01 — pour', '02 — shop', '03 — gather') set in Fraunces italic at 8rem, half-bleeding off the left margin like a manuscript folio
Handwritten-style SVG marginalia: small ink-drawn grape, cork, or flame motifs as section accents (1px stroke, beeswax color), never as bullets
Fractal-noise grain overlay at 0.04 opacity across the whole site to give a warm film-photograph texture, killing the flat-digital sheen

imagery.direction: Low-light, available-candlelight photography only: hands pouring, half-full glasses catching flame, cork detail, the bar at golden hour. No stock, no overhead flat-lays of cheese boards, no people-laughing-with-perfect-teeth.
imagery.treatment: Duotone in oxblood/beeswax for editorial moments; full-color but grain-overlaid for bottle hero shots. All images get a soft inner vignette and sit inside hairline 1px frames the color of the muted plum, never rounded more than 4px.

voice: Warm, candid, a little poetic. Talks about wine the way you'd describe a record you love — 'it's funky, kind of like cider's weirder cousin' — not 'notes of brett and volatile acidity.' Short sentences. Specific producers, specific villages. Never uses 'curated,' 'elevated,' or 'experience.' Will admit when a bottle is weird.

sections.intent: Oversized italic headline ('natural wine, *honestly*'), one-line subhead, mono kicker with hours + neighborhood, two CTAs (Reserve a tasting / See what's open tonight). Single oxblood candle-glow gradient.
Horizontal hairline-bento of 4–6 bottles currently open by the glass, with vintage numerals, producer, one-line plain-English tasting note. Updates weekly.
Two-column editorial: left is a 62ch letter explaining what natural wine is and isn't, right is a duotone photo of the bar. No jargon.
Inverted tone band, oversized numeral '02', this Thursday's theme, a paragraph from the host, and a Reserve button with amber glow on hover.
Names the current resident kitchen, links to their IG, lists three dishes in italic. Changes monthly, signals we're community-rooted.
Two real pull-quotes: one from SF press naming us best new wine bar, one from a regular. Set as oversized italic pull quotes, attributed in mono.
Address, hours grid (Tue–Sun evenings), map link, IG handle @vespera, email, a single line: 'walk-ins welcome, candle seats fill up.'
Headline ('~120 bottles, all worth opening'), kicker explaining we rotate constantly and you can take any of them home at retail.

Left sticky rail with plain-language filters (orange, pet-nat, 'weird and worth it', under $30, splurge). Right is a hairline-bento grid of bottles with vintage as serif numeral, producer mono kicker, region, and a one-sentence note in our voice.
Three featured bottles with a longer paragraph each — written by name, from whoever picked it. Photo in duotone, signed at the bottom.
Soft CTA card: 'tell us what you had and liked, we'll pick something' — opens a short email form, very low-friction.
Oversized italic 'gather around something open' with kicker 'thursdays, 7pm, eight seats.' One candle-glow accent.
Vertical list of next 4 tastings: oversized serif date numeral on left, theme + host paragraph on right, Reserve button per row. Sold-out states use a soft strikethrough in plum.
Three-up: 'eight people', 'six pours', 'two hours' — set as hairline-bento with oversized numerals. Below, a paragraph from the host explaining the vibe in plain words.
Inverted band, short pitch for buying out the bar (birthdays, anniversaries, small teams), single email CTA.
Single column, 62ch, signed and dated. Opens with why we started in 2021, what 'low-intervention' means to us, who we want in the room.

Three short stacked definitions in editorial style: 'farmed without chemicals', 'fermented with what's there', 'bottled without makeup.' Each with a one-line caveat — we're honest about the messy edges.
Portraits in duotone of the small team — two or three people — with handwritten-style captions about what each of them drinks at home.
Three photographs of the bar at different hours, full-color with grain. No copy. Just the space.
Repeat of visit footer with hello@vespera.demo, @vespera, hours, and the line 'come say hi.'
